attrs.management_says: No explanation for 2015 operating cash flow decline in provided MD&A excerpts. Prior year (2014) decline attributed to inventory and AR increases (E47). Forward-looking risks mention weather, order cancellations, ERP transition (E30, E31).
attrs.numbers_show: Operating cash flow fell 49% to $95.1M from $185.8M while net income rose 27% to $174.3M (E6, E16, E17, E24). The $90.7M CFO drop vs $37.1M net income rise implies ~$128M adverse working capital/non-cash changes. AR increased $27.6M; current liabilities fell $7M; current assets fell $16.6M overall, suggesting inventory/other current assets declined (source of cash), so other factors (e.g., tax payments, non-current working capital, ERP disruption) likely drove the CFO decline.

attrs.reason: The evidence pack contains no management explanation for the 49% decline in operating cash flow (from $185.8M to $95.1M) despite a 27% rise in net income (E6, E16, E17, E24). The 2014 MD&A attributed a CFO decline to inventory and AR increases (E47), but the 2015 MD&A excerpts (E30, E31) only mention forward-looking risks (weather, ERP transition) without addressing the 2015 CFO drop. A detailed working capital reconciliation (inventory, accounts payable, tax payments, etc.) is not provided. Therefore, the explanation is absent from the pack and remains unverified.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 49% decline in operating cash flow despite a 27% rise in net income likely reflects a combination of (1) the May 2015 ERP implementation in international distributor businesses (E30) which may have temporarily slowed billing and cash collections in the second half, (2) seasonal working capital patterns where heavy Q3 shipments (E27) lead to receivables buildup that is collected in Q4, and (3) possible higher tax payments or other non-recurring cash outflows not detailed in the provided summary. A full reconciliation requires a detailed working capital breakdown (inventory, accounts payable, tax payments) that is not present in the evidence pack.
